$comment: Gzipped byte budget for each shipped entry (keys: package, or package/subpath). Bumping a number requires intent. Current sizes captured 2026-05-22 with ~15% headroom above measured; extension-block-controls (formerly extension-block-menu) bumped 2026-06-08 for the unified drop-slot model, to be lowered once dist is minified; extension-block-controls bumped again 2026-08-02 for the drag-preview paint-style copy, which the spec requires because getComputedStyle().cssText is empty; extension-block-menu is now a thin deprecation shim that re-exports extension-block-controls; extension-image bumped 2026-08-04 for the align placement (second attribute, command and bubble item set). core bumped 2026-08-20 for the bubble menu's item pipeline, which moved into core from the four wrappers; the entry below records the measurements.
$comment-completeness: angular, theme and the twelve pm subpaths were added 2026-08-19, when the gate started discovering entries from each package's exports map instead of iterating these keys and assuming packages/<name>/dist/index.js. Nothing about the format changed: the same flat map of key to gzipped bytes, and every value above is the value it already had. Those fourteen entries simply had no ceiling before, so @domternal/theme's stylesheet, which every consumer loads, could grow without limit and the gate would still pass. The new numbers keep roughly a tenth of headroom over the measurement, the same convention as the rest of the file: angular 24650, theme 13992. The pm subpaths share one flat 70, a tenth above the largest of the twelve, because each is a single re-export line of 54 to 61 bytes where the gzip container itself is a third of the measurement: twelve separate numbers would churn on a rename without telling anyone anything, while one shared ceiling still catches a shim that stops being a shim.
$comment-core-2026-08-20: core 80000 to 82000. The bubble menu's item resolver (buildBubbleItemMaps, resolveBubbleMenuItems, resolveBubbleNames, detectBubbleContext, filterBubbleItemsBySchema, getBubbleFormatItems, collapseSeparators, createBubbleShouldShow) moved into core, where all four wrappers read it instead of each carrying a transcription of it. Measured: core 78765 to 80220, so +1455; vanilla 20997 to 19653, react 18636 to 17263, vue 20084 to 18838, angular 24650 to 23398, so the four wrappers shed 5215 between them. An app ships core plus one wrapper, so a single-framework consumer pays between 82 and 209 bytes more and gets one implementation in place of four. Core was already at 98 percent of its old ceiling before any of this, so the next addition of any size was going to trip the gate; the new number is the measurement plus about two percent.
